_comment: Curation manifest — declarative sampling, not a hand-listed set.
'seed' makes stratified selection reproducible. Agent-volume selection is fully
agent_volume — rank agents by how many conversations they have, then take up to
'max_per_agent' from each, busiest first, until 'count' is reached. The cap is
what keeps the set usable in both directions: without it the top one or two
agents swallow the whole budget (one twcs agent has 1,954 threads), leaving too
few agents to compare. At 10 you get ~10 agents with ~10 conversations each.
so the last agent usually pushes the total slightly past 'count'.
Use this when the work is per-agent: scorecards, comparison, improvement.
stratified — spread picks evenly across a neutral stratum (task / flow / domain).
Guarantees coverage of every interaction type. Use this when the work is about
the interactions rather than the people handling them.
ABCD carries no agent identity of any kind, so it cannot use agent_volume and is
stratified by flow instead. The build says so when it runs.
Filters are structural only — enough turns to be a conversation, both speakers
present, a complete transcript. Nothing about content or quality.
'pinned' forces specific conversations into the set regardless of sampling.
